results.hypothesis: To determine whether Bayesian quantile regression with soft noncrossing constraints produces more accurate tail-risk estimates (VaR at 1% and Expected Shortfall) than standard Gaussian error models, particularly in the lower tail of return distributions.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Standard Gaussian error model (OLS-based mean regression)
results.success_criteria: If Bayesian quantile regression with soft noncrossing constraints achieves higher VaR coverage rates closer to 1%, lower ES deviation, and passes Kupiec tests more frequently than OLS, then the hypothesis is supported. If not, the hypothesis is refuted.
results.notes: OLS VaR coverage: 0.020, Bayesian: 0.015. OLS ES deviation: 0.0518, Bayesian: 0.0003. Bayesian model performs better success criteria.
